item.subject: science
item.stem:
During a school geography lesson in Chennai, Meera reads that a cyclone developed over the warm waters of the Bay of Bengal. Her teacher asks the class how such a storm forms and what the region at its centre, called the eye, is like.
Which row of the table correctly describes the formation of the cyclone and the conditions in its eye compared with the surrounding region?

options.A: Warm moist air rises over the warm ocean and water vapour condenses; the eye is a calm, lowest-pressure region while surrounding areas have strong winds and heavy rain
options.B: Warm moist air rises over the warm ocean and water vapour condenses; the eye has the strongest winds and heaviest rain of the whole storm
options.C: Cyclones form just as readily over cold ocean water; the eye is a calm, lowest-pressure region while surrounding areas have strong winds and heavy rain
options.D: Cold dry air sinks over the warm ocean to start the storm; the eye is calm but at the highest pressure in the storm
